section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: FileCore has been updated to provide access to larger discs and to avoid limitations of the earlier interfaces.

swi-definition.name: FileCore_DiscOp64
swi-definition.description: Perform a disc operation using 64-bit disc addresses

entry.register-use:
Flags:
Reason code (see FileCore_DiscOp) Options (see FileCore_DiscOp) Reserved, must be 0

Pointer to disc address buffer:
Drive and flags:
Drive number (only drives 0-7 supported) Reserved, must be 0
Disc byte address (low 32 bits) Disc byte address (high 32 bits)
Pointer to alternative disc record, or 0 if unused
Cache handle, if relevant to the reason code
Pointer to FileCore instance private word

exit.register-use: Preserved (the block at R2 is updated to the next disc byte address)
Pointer to end of used buffer

use.p: This SWI is an extended form of FileCore_DiscOp which avoids limited 26bit interfaces. It is implemented internally within FileCore using the existing calls, thus the limitations are identical to those of the FileCore_DiscOp and FileCore_SectorOp calls. Future versions of the module may remove these limitations.

swi-definition.name: FileCore_Features
swi-definition.description: Read the feature set of the FileCore module

exit.register-use:
Feature flags:
FileCore modules should use new error scheme Reserved

use.p: This SWI is used to read the feature set of the FileCore module. If it returns an error, the feature flags should be assumed to be 0. At present FileCore does not support the extended error scheme and bit 0 will be clear. The scheme will be documented in a future release.
